quote.translation: The true contingency that sets the player's heart pounding lies, rather, in the force of the first push itself: in the fact that the determinate strength given as fact does not necessarily possess absolute necessity, that we think it could also have been some other strength, that is, in the fact that no contradiction whatever arises if we think of it as some other strength.

regions.text: も存しないといふ點に存するのである。

quote.translation: Let us take horse racing as a further concrete example.

regions.text: 具體な例を更に競馬にとつて考へて見よう。

quote.translation: That horse racing is one kind of what is called "winning and losing by chance" cannot be disputed.

regions.text: 競馬が謂はゆる「偶然の輸赢」の一種であることは争ばれない。もちろん競馬から偶然を除外しょうとする傾向がないとは云へない。

quote.translation: Of course, it cannot be said that there is no tendency to try to exclude chance from horse racing.

quote.translation: According to Kikuchi Kan's "My Philosophy of Betting Tickets" (carried in Hanashi, published by Bungei Shunjū-sha, May issue, Shōwa 10), "A dividend that is the result of good judgement brings great satisfaction, whether the amount is large or small.

regions.text: まくれ御かの配當はたとひ二百囲なりとを授機師にして正道なる馬姿ファンの手柄にすべきものにあらず』「百二三十圓の穴にても手柄の上では二百園に當るものあり。二百圓の配償にても手柄の上ではくだらぬものあり。

quote.translation: The dividend from a fluke, even if it is two hundred yen, is speculative, and is nothing a proper betting-ticket fan should count to his credit"; "Even a long shot of a hundred and twenty or thirty yen may be worth two hundred yen in credit, and even a dividend of two hundred yen may be worth nothing in credit.

regions.text: 新馬の二百囲をまくれ御加に取りたるなどただ金を撤つたのとあまり迷はない」『サラブ、レッドとは、如何なるものかも知らずに馬券をやる人あり悲しむべし腸

quote.translation: Taking two hundred yen on a new horse by a fluke is not much different from simply picking up money"; and "There are people who bet without even knowing what a thoroughbred is, which is to be lamented.

regions.text: の血紙記嫁などをちつとも研究せずに馬券をやるのは応くお扣である』

quote.translation: To bet without the least study of the horses' bloodlines, records and so on is to be a gambler."

regions.text: 論者は競馬を偶然の遊戲として享楽することには反對のやうに見える。

quote.translation: The writer appears to be opposed to enjoying horse racing as a play of chance.

regions.text: 『同期開催濟の各競馬の成績を丹念に調べよ。そのお蔭で大穴を一つ二つは取れるも

quote.translation: "Examine carefully the results of each race at the same meeting, and thanks to that you will be able to take one or two big long shots ."
